tests.name: Windows Disable LSA Protection
tests.description:
The following Atomic adds a registry entry to disable LSA Protection.

The LSA controls and manages user rights information, password hashes and other important bits of information in memory. Attacker tools, such as mimikatz, rely on accessing this content to scrape password hashes or clear-text passwords. Enabling LSA Protection configures Windows to control the information stored in memory in a more secure fashion - specifically, to prevent non-protected processes from accessing that data.
Upon successful execution, the registry will be modified and RunAsPPL will be set to 0, disabling Lsass protection.
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/security/credentials-protection-and-ma

tests.name: Disable Windows Defender with DISM
tests.description:
The following Atomic will attempt to disable Windows-Defender using the built in DISM.exe, Deployment Image Servicing and Management tool. 
DISM is used to enumerate, install, uninstall, configure, and update features and packages in Windows images.
A successful execution will not standard-out any details. Remove the quiet switch if verbosity is needed.
This method will remove Defender and it's package.

- Uses built-in Windows QoS features to manipulate application bandwidth
- Limits network throughput to extremely low levels (e.g., 8 bits per second)
- Causes security agents to repeatedly time out when attempting to communicate with their cloud backend

tests.description:
Patches AmsiScanBuffer in memory using P/Invoke to resolve the function address via

return AMSI_RESULT_CLEAN immediately (mov al, 1; ret).

Reference: https://i.blackhat.com/briefings/asia/2018/asia-18-Tal-Liberman-Documenting-the-Undocumented-The-Rise-and-Fall-of-AMSI.pdf

tests.name: Impair Windows Defender via Disk Space Exhaustion using fsutil
tests.description:
Simulates defense impairment by leveraging the built-in Windows utility fsutil.exe to create an arbitrary oversized hidden file in the user %TEMP% directory.
In real-world evasion (e.g., BigDiskBuster technique), adversaries size a hidden GUID-named file to consume all available free disk space on the system drive. This condition causes Microsoft Defender Antivirus platform updates and dynamic signature downloads to fail due to disk exhaustion (ERROR_DISK_FULL / 0x80070070), freezing definition updates while keeping nominal services running.

This test creates a non-destructive temporary test file to validate detection telemetry without crashing the system drive.

References:
- https://lolba
